The axis is applicant. Register: "Grupo Epelsa S.L." Document: "Grupo Epelsa S.L.U."

This is a legal-suffix drift — S.L. vs S.L.U. (Sociedad Limitada vs Sociedad Limitada Unipersonal). Per rules, legal-suffix drift = same-entity. Best value: hmm — for same-entity, what's the best value? The rules say for same-entity cases like number/year format differences, use register's canonical form. For spelling drift/suffix drift same-entity, the best value — the fused record should probably carry the document's fuller form or the register's canonical form? The rules explicitly say "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." For spelling drift, they don't specify, but document is the legal instrument... However, the register is the OIML-CS database, which is authoritative for the register id. For suffix drift, S.L.U. is a fuller legal form; the document is the legal instrument, so arguably the document's value is more legally precise. But the rule for different-entity explicitly says best_value = document's since certificate is legal instrument; for same-entity no explicit rule. I'd say best_value = document's "Grupo Epelsa S.L.U." because the certificate document is the legal instrument and S.L.U. is the more complete legal designation. Alternatively register canonical.

Hmm. Let me think about what a fusion system would do. For same-entity with spelling drift, typically prefer the document (primary source, legal instrument) unless it's noise. The rules only override to register for number format canonicalization and document-noise. So for same-entity drift, best_value = document's value. I'll go with "Grupo Epelsa S.L.U." — verdict same-entity.
